To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
more specialized university output production, as measured by profit efficiency, yields higher financial ratios on average than less specialised university production.
the profit efficiency of a university is a function of the specialization of its output, and this relationship is robust to the modelling approach used.

(i) the average profit efficiency of UK universities is relatively high; (ii) the profit efficiency of more specialized universities is higher than the profit efficiency of less specialized universities; and (iii) nonparametric modelling using financial ratios is more useful than nonparametric modelling of prices and quantities for this profit efficiency issue in UK higher education.

a new approach to the benchmarking of UK higher education and the use of profit efficiency to inform policy.

the use of profit efficiency and financial ratios modelling for the benchmarking of UK higher education is a promising avenue to be further explored.
the nonparametric profit efficiency methodology is an appropriate tool for best-practice benchmark in higher education.

nonparametric modelling using financial ratios is a useful complement to nonparametric models based on prices and quantities, and can provide a more accessible way of understanding the performance of universities.

, in terms of best-practice benchmark, nonparametric modelling of profit efficiency with financial ratios is more useful for policy analysis than nonparametric modelling using the prices and quantities for each university's inputs/outputs, at least for the UK university sector.

the profit efficiency of universities can be used to inform the policy debate on the appropriate degree of specialization in the university sector.
